claim_summary: Frantzman acknowledges that settler origins are central to new-village formation and that Arab/Muslim immigration into Palestine is contentious.
quoted_text: Understanding the process that led to new village formation in Palestine requires also an understanding of where the settlers came from... there are very contentious questions surrounding the amount of Arab and Muslim immigration to Palestine during the 19th and 20th centuries.
page_or_ref: Frantzman 2010, Origins of the new Settlers 1871-1922
notes: Use to justify re-coding origins rather than accepting broad local/external categories.

claim_summary: Frantzman states that new village origins do not necessarily indicate outside-Palestine origins except in cases of migrating Bedouin tribes and two unique Muslim-refugee villages.
quoted_text: an examination of the origins of the settlers of many of the new villages does not indicate that they were necessarily from outside Palestine, except in the cases of migrating Bedouin tribes and two unique villages established by Muslim refugees.
page_or_ref: Frantzman 2010, Origins of the new Settlers 1871-1922
notes: This sentence creates the key research target: migrating Bedouin tribes and Muslim-refugee villages.

claim_summary: Fischel and Kark document failed, abandoned, or absorbed refugee settlements, supporting a settlement-survival-bias critique.
quoted_text: Bosnian refugees deserted two Sharon sites due to fever; Khirbat al-Sarkas/al-Ghaba was deserted before the 1930s and later resettled; Zayta may have been abandoned after one or two years.
notes: Use as evidence that surviving settlements understate movement.
